requirement:
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:none` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:

> Cite this only when no requirement or example applies to the item under the
> reference procedure. The citation MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST
> justify why the item exists. An item with an invariant worth checking, such as
> a cache that must not change results, needs a requirement stating that
> invariant instead. An item citing this MUST NOT implement end-user-observable
> behavior that no requirement specifies.

Only `{cite}` MAY reference it. Validation MUST report an inline citation of it
or a fenced citation whose body, without comment delimiters and other
references, is empty. Whether the justification holds MUST be assessed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. `habeas status --all` MUST list
each `habeas:none` citation with its item and justification.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.references.no_requirement`.

**Obligations, code and tests**

1. **Provide the built-in `habeas:none` with the stated text (MUST).**
   - Code: `BUILTINS` in `src/builtins.rs` declares it with only the `Cite` role and `requires_justification: true`. `Builtin::text` in `src/builtins.rs` takes its text from the requirement's own quoted block in `md/requirements/references.md`.
   - Test: `habeas_none_has_its_approved_text_and_only_permits_fenced_citations` in `src/builtins.rs` checks the start and end of the text. It also asserts the text equals the quote in `md/reference.md`, which covers the documentation of the text.
   - Test: `fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked` in `src/lib.rs` cites `builtin_definitions`, not this requirement. It also checks that the badge's hover text is the built-in's text.

2. **Validation reports an inline citation (MUST).**
   - Code: `validate_references` in `src/evidence.rs` calls `Builtin::check` with `commentary = None`. That returns "must be cited in fenced form".
   - Test: `tests/references.rs`, `fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated`, asserts the error at `src/lib.rs:6`.

3. **Validation reports a fenced citation whose body is empty once comment delimiters and other references are removed (MUST).**
   - Code: `Builtin::check` calls `fenced::justification`, which strips inline references, nested fence lines and whitespace.
   - Test: `justification_excludes_references_and_nested_fences` in `src/fenced.rs`, plus the `src/lib.rs:9` assertion in the `tests/references.rs` test above. The builtins unit test also checks the "empty justification" error.

4. **Only `{cite}` may reference it (MAY).** This imposes nothing to check. `Builtin::check` still rejects other roles. That is tested at `src/lib.rs:14` and in the book case `md/rules.md:9`.

5. **Whether the justification holds is assessed under `citation_review` (MUST).**
   - Code: `prepare_citation` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs` supplies the built-in text as a mandatory input via `builtin_input`. Step 3 of the citation prompt, in `md/requirements/authoring.md`, checks the justification, whether any requirement applies, and unspecified end-user-observable behavior.
   - Code: `missing_function_references` in `src/rust_coverage.rs` counts a `habeas:none` citation as a reference only if `check` accepts it. It carries an `{impl}` to this requirement.
   - Tests: `citation_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_the_item_and_citations` (`src/authoring/mod.rs`) and `citation_review_inputs_combine_item_declarations_terms_and_built_ins_once` (`src/authoring/inputs.rs`) assert that the built-in text is a mandatory input. Both carry `{test}` references to `citation_review`, not to this requirement.
   - The review mechanism is covered by `citation_review` and `citation_prompt`. I did not reassess those requirements here.

6. **`habeas status --all` lists each `habeas:none` citation with its item and justification (MUST).**
   - Code: `none_citations` in `src/citations.rs`, and the `if all` block in `status_markdown_with_github` in `src/commands.rs`. The `if all` block prints the file, selector, line and whitespace-normalised justification.
   - Test: `status_all_lists_habeas_none_citations_with_their_justification` asserts the exact output with `--all`. It also asserts the section is absent without `--all`, so both paths are tested.

7. **An item citing it MUST NOT implement unspecified behavior; the citation must use the fenced form with a justifying body.** These are carried by the fixed built-in text and enforced through validation (item 3) and the citation review (item 5).

**Marking and unspecified behavior**
- I found no code implementing this requirement without an `{impl}` reference. `validate_references`, `check`, `justification`, `none_citations`, the status function, `BUILTINS` and `text` are all marked.
- I found no unmarked tests.
- The error messages and the "## `habeas:none` citations" heading are wording and layout chosen for output the text requires, so they are specified behavior.

No `{fixme}` references are involved.

Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:none` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this only when no requirement or example applies to the item under the
> reference procedure. The citation MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST
> justify why the item exists. An item with an invariant worth checking, such as
> a cache that must not change results, needs a requirement stating that
> invariant instead. An item citing this MUST NOT implement end-user-observable
> behavior that no requirement specifies.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it. Validation MUST report an inline citation of it
or a fenced citation whose body, without comment delimiters and other
references, is empty. Whether the justification holds MUST be assessed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. `habeas status --all` MUST list
each `habeas:none` citation with its item and justification.
:::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. The reviewer MUST assess, for each citation,
whether the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition
changes, and whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead;
for `habeas:none`, whether its justification is true, no definition applies, and
the item implements no unspecified end-user-observable behavior. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
